authors: Celio Boulay, with Dylan Sparrow and Rafael Castro
title: expander-graphs, explained
h1: Expander graphs in Lean 4: a finished expander mixing lemma, and the start of Fan Chung's spectral graph theory
lead: The finished centrepiece is the expander mixing lemma. In a connected d-regular graph whose normalised adjacency eigenvalues, apart from the top one, are all at most γ in size, any two vertex sets A and B have almost exactly the number of edges between them that a random graph would have: the error is at most γ·d·√(|A||B|). Its proof is complete in the source. The Chung-style chapters around it are a work in progress: several key statements end in sorry, and by our reading the Cheeger constant, as currently defined, is 0 for every graph.
desc: An unofficial plain-English tour of Celio Boulay's Lean 4 project on expander graphs: a complete expander mixing lemma, a greedy colouring bound, and work-in-progress definitions from Fan Chung's Spectral Graph Theory (normalised Laplacian, connectivity, Cheeger constant), several of them still sorry'd.
startNote: Start with the finished result, the expander mixing lemma, and the two ideas it rests on: what “γ-expander” means here and why the eigenvalue 1 is simple. Then look at the Chung-style material: the normalised Laplacian, why 0 is always one of its eigenvalues, and the unfinished Cheeger bound. The greedy colouring bound is a self-contained side file.
sizeNote: About 1,340 lines of Lean in 6 files under ExpanderGraphs/, plus a LaTeX blueprint. It targets Lean 4.31 (release candidate) with Mathlib.
agentCtx: A work-in-progress Lean 4 + Mathlib formalisation of expander graphs and Fan Chung's spectral graph theory: a complete expander mixing lemma, a greedy colouring bound, and partly sorry'd results on the normalised Laplacian and the Cheeger constant.
